chapter: New York, the Kentucky Club and the high-hat
title: Gangsters want the band for the Cotton Club
summary: The band is told to enlarge and move to the Cotton Club; Greer resists but Leo Bernstein sends him along.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I stayed down there-- we got so popular, the guys the gangsters bought the Cotton Club, they said, 'I want that band.' What you going to say, when they say I want something they get it. When they told Duke we got to augment the band, make the band larger and go to the Cotton Club, I said man, 'I ain't going up there,' and he said come on. I said I ain't going. I ain't going, so I told Leo I'm going to stay here, let them go, and he said, 'No, you better go.' Because he know. 'I will miss you guys, but you go ahead.'

So I went up there and I wasn't -- it was all right, so when I got up there, it was a big place and the Cotton Club was the rage then. If you come to New York and didn't go to the Cotton Club, you wasn't nowhere, so I went up there and so now, in the meantime, I was the drum designer for a company out of Elkhart, Indiana called Lezy Drum Manufacturing, one of the biggest.
